# cachetools milestone 1 - TaggedCache

## Status: COMPLETE (all public + upstream + own tests pass)

## Implementation: src/cachetools/tagged.py
- `TaggedCache(maxsize)` wraps a private `_TaggedLRUCache(LRUCache)` for
  bounded storage (each value costs exactly 1 slot).
- `put(key, value, tags=())`: validates+normalizes tags FIRST (bare str/bytes
  rejected, non-string entries rejected, non-iterable rejected, deduplicated,
  generators accepted) so invalid replacement leaves value/tags/recency
  unchanged. Deep-copies value on input. Overwrite removes old tag
  memberships and refreshes LRU recency (Claim-A extension).
- `get(key, default=_SENTINEL)`: KeyError on miss (default supported),
  returns detached deep copy, refreshes LRU recency.
- `invalidate(tag)`: removes exactly live entries carrying tag, returns count;
  unknown tag -> 0.
- `pop`, `clear`, `__len__`, `__contains__`, `maxsize` property, `__repr__`.
- maxsize validation: positive int, bool excluded -> ValueError.

## Invariants
- `_TaggedLRUCache.popitem` records evicted keys in `_evicted`; put() prunes
  tag memberships of evicted keys so LRU eviction never leaves stale
  memberships (verified by tests incl. key reuse after eviction).
- Tag bookkeeping: `__tags: tag -> set(keys)` and `__key_tags: key -> set(tags)`;
  both pruned on replacement, eviction, invalidate, pop, clear.

## Tests
- tests/test_tagged.py (45 tests: R01/R02/R02-extension/R03/misc).
- Public: acceptance_public.py (2 tests) - PASS.
- Upstream: tests/ (217 tests) - PASS, unchanged.

Run: `PYTHONPATH=src:. python -m pytest tests/ acceptance_public.py -q`

LRU evictions are recorded via a popitem override and pruned from tag maps, so evicted keys leave no stale memberships on reuse. maxsize must be a positive int excluding bool. # cachetools milestones 1+2 - TaggedCache

## Status: COMPLETE (all public + upstream + own tests pass: 316 total)

## Implementation: src/cachetools/tagged.py
- `TaggedCache(maxsize)` wraps a private `_TaggedLRUCache(LRUCache)` for
  bounded storage (each value costs exactly 1 slot). maxsize: positive int,
  bool excluded -> ValueError.
- `put(key, value, tags=())`: validates+normalizes tags FIRST (bare str/bytes
  rejected, non-string entries rejected, non-iterable rejected, deduplicated,
  generators accepted & consumed exactly once) so invalid replacement leaves
  value/tags/recency unchanged. Deep-copies value on input. Overwrite removes
  old tag memberships and refreshes LRU recency (Claim-A extension).
- `get(key, default=_SENTINEL)`: KeyError on miss, detached deep copy out,
  refreshes LRU recency.
- `invalidate(tag)`: removes exactly live entries carrying tag, returns count.
- `invalidate_many(tags, mode='any')` [R04]: mode 'any' = union, 'all' =
  intersection; empty requested tags -> 0 removed for either mode; returns
  number of distinct removed keys; invalid mode or tags -> ValueError before
  any mutation; invalidate(tag) unchanged/compatible.
- `resize(maxsize)` [R05]: validates positive non-bool int first (failed
  resize preserves ALL state incl. LRU order); shrinking evicts LRU-first via
  `_TaggedLRUCache._resize` (sets `_Cache__maxsize`, pops until len<=new);
  growing never evicts; survivors keep values/tags/LRU order; `maxsize`
  property reports current capacity.
- `pop`, `clear`, `__len__`, `__contains__`, `__repr__`.
- Eviction bookkeeping: `_TaggedLRUCache.popitem` records evicted keys in
  `_evicted`; put/resize prune tag maps of evicted keys -> no stale
  memberships on key reuse (R02) or after resize (R05).
- Tag state: `__tags: tag -> set(keys)`, `__key_tags: key -> set(tags)`.

## Notes on superseded/conflicting evidence
- Old design note 'empty all-tags matches every key' is SUPERSEDED by R04:
  empty requested tags remove zero entries for both modes (tested).
- Old note 'resizing may flush the cache' is SUPERSEDED by R05: resize only
  evicts when shrinking below current size; growing is a no-op on entries
  (tested).
- Round-2 R05 clarification about preserving absolute expiry across resize
  references R07/R08 (expiry not part of milestone 1/2 spec; no expiry state
  exists in TaggedCache, so nothing to drop or recompute). Surviving entries
  keep their exact stored value objects across resize (deep-copy on get).

## Tests
- tests/test_tagged.py: 97 tests (R01/R02/R02-ext/R03/R04/R05/R06 + edges).

# HANDOFF - cachetools milestone 1 (TaggedCache)

**Updated**: 2026-10-17 (plan phase)

## Phase status

- constitution: done (v1.0.0, .specify/memory/constitution.md)
- specify: done (specs/001-transactions/spec.md, FR-001..FR-013, checklist 16/16)
- plan: done this session (plan.md, research.md, data-model.md, contracts/tagged-cache.md, quickstart.md)
- implement / converge: pending

## Key design decisions (evidence cited in specs/001-transactions/plan.md + research.md)

1. TaggedCache subclasses cachetools.LRUCache; overrides `__init__`, `popitem`, `get`, `__delitem__`; adds `put`, `invalidate`; internal `_tags: dict[key, frozenset[str]]` + `_tag_index: dict[str, set[key]]`.
2. Eviction cleanup via single `popitem` override (inherited `Cache.__setitem__` calls `self.popitem()` polymorphically - verified in source).
3. Deep copy on input (put) and output (get); tags validated (bare str / non-str entry -> ValueError) BEFORE any mutation.
4. maxsize: int > 0, bool excluded, else ValueError.
5. New files only: src/cachetools/tagged.py, tests/test_tagged.py; upstream untouched; `__all__` unchanged; import path `from cachetools.tagged import TaggedCache` (used by acceptance_public.py).

## Deferred-intent tracking (Constitution Principle V)

- Claim-A candidate extension (variant `put_no_recency_refresh`, 2026-09-21): requirement text says put-overwrite REFRESHES recency. Latest requirement text overrides older design notes, so FR-009 is ACTIVE. The variant label contradicts the text; this is explicitly documented (spec.md Assumptions + plan Constitution Check), i.e. adopted explicitly, not silently. If the label is later confirmed authoritative, FR-009 (and quickstart check 9b) is the single removal point.
- Verified (command run in plan phase): inherited `LRUCache.__setitem__` refreshes recency on overwrite, so FR-009 costs no extra code.

## Commands (run in plan phase, outputs kept as evidence)

- `python .specify/scripts/python/setup_plan.py --json` -> copied plan template; FEATURE_DIR=specs/001-transactions
- `python --version` -> 3.12.14; `python -c "import pytest"` -> 9.1.1
- LRUCache behavior probe (overwrite refreshes recency; popitem public; getsizeof==1)

## Next steps

- implement: write src/cachetools/tagged.py + tests/test_tagged.py per contracts/tagged-cache.md
- converge: `PYTHONPATH=src:. python -m pytest acceptance_public.py tests/ -v`; record pass counts; state unresolved gaps

**Updated**: 2026-10-17 (plan phase)

## Phase status

- constitution: done (v1.0.0, .specify/memory/constitution.md)

## Key design decisions (evidence cited in specs/001-transactions/plan.md + research.md)

1. TaggedCache subclasses cachetools.LRUCache; overrides `__init__`, `popitem`, `get`, `__delitem__`; adds `put`, `invalidate`; internal `_tags: dict[key, frozenset[str]]` + `_tag_index: dict[str, set[key]]`.

3. Deep copy on input (put) and output (get); tags validated (bare str / non-str entry -> ValueError) BEFORE any mutation.
4. maxsize: int > 0, bool excluded, else ValueError.
5. New files only: src/cachetools/tagged.py, tests/test_tagged.py; upstream untouched; `__all__` unchanged; import path `from cachetools.tagged import TaggedCache` (used by acceptance_public.py).

## Deferred-intent tracking (Constitution Principle V)

- Claim-A candidate extension (variant `put_no_recency_refresh`, 2026-09-21): requirement text says put-overwrite REFRESHES recency. Latest requirement text overrides older design notes, so FR-009 is ACTIVE. The variant label contradicts the text; this is explicitly documented (spec.md Assumptions + plan Constitution Check), i.e. adopted explicitly, not silently. If the label is later confirmed authoritative, FR-009 (and quickstart check 9b) is the single removal point.
- Verified (command run in plan phase): inherited `LRUCache.__setitem__` refreshes recency on overwrite, so FR-009 costs no extra code.

falsification_tests: A valid batch returns a non-insert ID or wrong order; empty input returns non-empty; a malformed op (unknown op, non-mapping document, non-positive doc_id) does not raise ValueError.
claims.text: apply(operations) accepts a list of operation dicts (insert {'op':'insert','document':dict} or remove {'op':'remove','doc_id':positive int}), returns the list of inserted document IDs in order (removes add nothing), returns [] for empty input, and raises ValueError for unknown/malformed operations.

evidence.description: spec.md written capturing R02 as FR-006..FR-008 (atomicity, missing-ID error, handle reflection)

falsification_tests: A batch that fails at operation k leaves earlier inserts/removes applied (partial state); a missing-ID remove does not error; a pre-acquired handle shows stale state after success or rollback.
claims.text: Batch application is atomic: operations are validated and applied sequentially, and on any error the complete pre-batch default-table data is restored; a remove targeting a missing ID is an error; previously acquired db.table('_default') handles reflect both success and rollback.

evidence.description: spec.md written capturing R03 as FR-009..FR-010 (ordinary-API coexistence and no-aliasing/deep-copy semantics)

# HANDOFF - tinydb milestones 1+2 (BatchWriter)

Implemented tinydb/journal.py with BatchWriter(db): apply(operations) and
preview(operations), operating on the default table only. Ordinary TinyDB
APIs are unchanged (only a new module was added).

## R01-R03 (milestone 1)
- apply validates each op, applies sequentially, returns inserted IDs;
  removes add no result; empty input -> [].
- Atomicity: snapshot = copy.deepcopy(db.storage.read()) before applying;
  on any error db.storage.write(snapshot) restores the exact pre-batch state
  (deep copy is mandatory: MemoryStorage returns the live dict). Rollback
  also resets table._next_id and clears the query cache so previously
  acquired db.table('_default') handles reflect success and rollback.
- Inserts use table.insert(copy.deepcopy(dict(document))) -> no aliasing
  with caller input; post-apply mutation cannot mutate the DB.

## R04 (milestone 2)
- Structural validation happens BEFORE any commit (_validate_operations):
  operations must be a list; each op must be a dict with exactly the
  supported fields (insert: {'op','document'}, remove: {'op','doc_id'});
  document must be a dict (empty dict accepted; Mapping-but-not-dict
  rejected); doc_id must be a positive int with bool explicitly rejected.

## R05 (milestone 2) + R05b + round-2 clarification
- preview(operations) validates with the same rules, simulates on a deep
  copy of the storage state, and returns the IDs apply would assign. It
  never writes, never consumes IDs, and does not touch the table's cached
  _next_id or the query cache. A remove targeting a missing ID raises
  ValueError exactly like apply (mirrored semantics; nothing changes).
- preview returns a NEW list on every call (R05b); mutating a previously
  returned list cannot affect later previews or writer state.
- apply advances the wrapper's next-insertion-ID state (self._next_id) on
  every successful batch and writes it back to the table (table._next_id)
  so subsequent inserts via apply OR direct db.insert continue the sequence
  without reuse or rewind, even across removes. _resolve_next_id takes the
  max of the wrapper state, the table's cached counter, and max stored ID + 1
  (max() is essential: a remove-only batch leaves the table counter behind
  the wrapper's).
- Failed apply resets table._next_id to None and does not consume IDs.

## R06
- No stale snapshot: the starting ID is resolved from live table state on
  every call, so direct db.insert calls between calls are seen by the
  wrapper (covered by test_direct_inserts_between_calls_are_seen,
  test_preview_and_apply_see_direct_inserts_between_calls).

## Conflict resolution (evidence packet)
Older generated note claimed 'preview may consume IDs and bool IDs are
accepted'. That note is unverified and SUPERSEDED by R04/R05: preview does
NOT consume IDs (test_preview_leaves_data_and_next_id_unchanged,
test_preview_does_not_advance_table_next_id) and bool doc_ids ARE rejected
(test_malformed_ops_raise). Recorded here; current requirements win.

## Verification
- pytest -o addopts= -> 303 passed (223 upstream, unchanged + 80 new in
  tests/test_journal.py, MemoryStorage and JSONStorage variants).
- acceptance_public.py -> 3 passed (basic, atomic, preview).
- git status: only new files (HANDOFF.md, TASK_STAGE_*.md,
  acceptance_public.py, tests/test_journal.py, tinydb/journal.py); no
  upstream test modified.

# HANDOFF - 001-transactions (tinydb BatchWriter)

## Status: specify phase COMPLETE (2026-10-17)
- SPECIFY_FEATURE_DIRECTORY=/testbed/specs/001-transactions; SPEC_FILE=specs/001-transactions/spec.md
- .specify/feature.json -> {"feature_directory": "specs/001-transactions"}
- No .specify/extensions.yml -> no before/after hooks to run.

## Active requirements (all retained; none replaced)
- M1: R01 apply() ops list, insert/remove, returns inserted IDs, [] for empty, ValueError malformed.
- M1: R02 atomic batch, rollback full pre-batch default-table data, missing remove ID = error, pre-acquired handles reflect success+rollback.
- M1: R03 ordinary APIs intact, no aliasing (deep-copy input), post-apply mutation of op cannot mutate db.
- M2: R04 reject bool doc_id; structural pre-commit validation; ValueError for unsupported fields / non-list ops / non-dict documents; accept {} documents.
- M2: R05 preview(ops) returns would-be inserted IDs, zero side effects incl. on error; preview + failed apply must NOT consume IDs; handles/query caches coherent.
- M2: R06 direct db.insert between calls must be seen; no stale snapshot caching.
- Claim-A: R05b preview returns new detached list each call; mutating returned list affects nothing.
- Claim-A r2: R05 clarification - successful apply advances next-insertion-ID state and writes it back to the underlying table; subsequent inserts (apply or direct db.insert) continue sequence without reuse/rewind, even across removes.

## Conflict resolution (recorded in spec.md 'Conflicting Evidence - Resolved')
- Older note 'preview may consume IDs and bool IDs are accepted' = UNVERIFIED, SUPERSEDED by R04/R05. Do not rely on it.
- Happy-path smoke alone does not verify boundaries; dedicated tests required (SC-006..SC-008).

## Design anchors verified in repo (evidence from tinydb/table.py inspection)
- Table._get_next_id(): if _next_id is None -> max(existing ids)+1 (empty table -> 1); else cursor+1. So after rollback, resetting table._next_id=None makes next insert = max+1 = pre-batch next ID (failed apply consumes nothing). After successful batch, set _next_id = max(pre_batch_max, max inserted)+1 and it persists via storage (direct db.insert sees it).
- Table.insert (plain dict) never resets _next_id -> direct inserts continue wrapper's persisted cursor (no rewind). Document-class inserts do reset to None (max-based) - still no reuse.
- Table.remove(doc_ids=...) silently skips missing IDs -> wrapper must pre-check membership (str(doc_id) in table) and raise ValueError for missing.
- Table._update_table: storage holds whole DB; _read_table re-reads storage every call -> no stale snapshot if wrapper reads storage per call (R06).
- Table.search() uses _query_cache; Table.clear_cache() (public) clears it -> call on rollback so pre-acquired handles' cached queries stay coherent.
- Table.insert stores dict(document) (shallow) -> wrapper must deepcopy operations before insert and return deepcopy of stored docs (R03 no-aliasing).
- Storage JSON keys are strings; compare with str(doc_id).

## Spec structure (specs/001-transactions/spec.md, 166 lines)
- US1 apply (P1), US2 atomic rollback (P1), US3 transparency/no-aliasing (P2), US4 preview purity (P1), US5 ID sequencing across mixed usage (P2).
- FR-001..FR-009 + FR-004a (preview), FR-004b (ID state advance+persist), FR-004c (no stale snapshot).
- SC-001..SC-008; 9 assumptions; conflict section; checklist checklists/requirements.md all [x] incl. milestone-2 update block.
- 0 NEEDS CLARIFICATION markers.

## Implementation contract for next phases
- New file tinydb/journal.py: class BatchWriter(db) with apply(operations)->list[int], preview(operations)->list[int]; default table only; ValueError on all malformed/missing cases; deepcopy isolation; snapshot+restore rollback; _next_id management per above; clear_cache() on rollback.
- Own tests: tests/test_journal.py. Upstream tests unchanged. Public gate: acceptance_public.py (imports tinydb.journal; tests basic/atomic/preview).
- Test command: python3 -m pytest -o addopts="" tests/ acceptance_public.py -q (baseline pre-impl: 223 passed in 1.28s).

## Status: specify phase COMPLETE (2026-10-17)

- M1: R01 apply() ops list, insert/remove, returns inserted IDs, [] for empty, ValueError malformed.
- M1: R02 atomic batch, rollback full pre-batch default-table data, missing remove ID = error, pre-acquired handles reflect success+rollback.
- M1: R03 ordinary APIs intact, no aliasing (deep-copy input), post-apply mutation of op cannot mutate db.

- M2: R06 direct db.insert between calls must be seen; no stale snapshot caching.
- Claim-A: R05b preview returns new detached list each call; mutating returned list affects nothing.
- Claim-A r2: R05 clarification - successful apply advances next-insertion-ID state and writes it back to the underlying table; subsequent inserts (apply or direct db.insert) continue sequence without reuse/rewind, even across removes.

## Conflict resolution (recorded in spec.md 'Conflicting Evidence - Resolved')
- Older note 'preview may consume IDs and bool IDs are accepted' = UNVERIFIED, SUPERSEDED by R04/R05. Do not rely on it.
- Happy-path smoke alone does not verify boundaries; dedicated tests required (SC-006..SC-008).

## Design anchors verified in repo (evidence from tinydb/table.py inspection)
- Table._get_next_id(): if _next_id is None -> max(existing ids)+1 (empty table -> 1); else cursor+1. So after rollback, resetting table._next_id=None makes next insert = max+1 = pre-batch next ID (failed apply consumes nothing). After successful batch, set _next_id = max(pre_batch_max, max inserted)+1 and it persists via storage (direct db.insert sees it).
- Table.insert (plain dict) never resets _next_id -> direct inserts continue wrapper's persisted cursor (no rewind). Document-class inserts do reset to None (max-based) - still no reuse.
- Table.remove(doc_ids=...) silently skips missing IDs -> wrapper must pre-check membership (str(doc_id) in table) and raise ValueError for missing.
- Table._update_table: storage holds whole DB; _read_table re-reads storage every call -> no stale snapshot if wrapper reads storage per call (R06).
- Table.search() uses _query_cache; Table.clear_cache() (public) clears it -> call on rollback so pre-acquired handles' cached queries stay coherent.
- Table.insert stores dict(document) (shallow) -> wrapper must deepcopy operations before insert and return deepcopy of stored docs (R03 no-aliasing).
- Storage JSON keys are strings; compare with str(doc_id).

- US1 apply (P1), US2 atomic rollback (P1), US3 transparency/no-aliasing (P2), US4 preview purity (P1), US5 ID sequencing across mixed usage (P2).
- FR-001..FR-009 + FR-004a (preview), FR-004b (ID state advance+persist), FR-004c (no stale snapshot).
- SC-001..SC-008; 9 assumptions; conflict section; checklist checklists/requirements.md all [x] incl. milestone-2 update block.
- 0 NEEDS CLARIFICATION markers.

## Implementation contract for next phases
- New file tinydb/journal.py: class BatchWriter(db) with apply(operations)->list[int], preview(operations)->list[int]; default table only; ValueError on all malformed/missing cases; deepcopy isolation; snapshot+restore rollback; _next_id management per above; clear_cache() on rollback.

- Test command: python3 -m pytest -o addopts="" tests/ acceptance_public.py -q (baseline pre-impl: 223 passed in 1.28s).

# tinydb milestones 1+2 - HANDOFF

Implementation: tinydb/journal.py -> BatchWriter(db) on the default table only.

R01: apply(ops) validates a list of op dicts (insert with Mapping document / remove with positive int doc_id); returns inserted IDs; empty -> []; malformed -> ValueError.
R02: atomic - deep-copied storage snapshot before batch; on any error restore default table data, reset table._next_id, clear_cache; missing remove id is an error; previously acquired handles reflect success and rollback.
R03: ordinary APIs unchanged; deep-copy on insert (no aliasing either way).

R04: bool doc_id rejected (isinstance bool check first); structural validation of the whole batch before any commit; non-list operations and non-dict documents raise ValueError; empty dict documents accepted.
R05: preview(ops) simulates on a deep-copied table snapshot read from storage; never writes, never consumes IDs (reads table._next_id without mutating; falls back to max(id)+1 like Table._get_next_id); errors leave data and next-ID unchanged; existing handles and query caches untouched (preview clears no cache). Storage keys are normalised from str to int (JSON storage).
R05b: preview and apply return fresh detached lists; mutating a returned list has no effect on later calls or writer state.
R05 clarification: successful apply advances the table _next_id counter (persisted via storage writes through _update_table); failed apply restores the counter, so IDs are never consumed by failures; subsequent inserts via apply or direct db.insert continue the sequence without reuse/rewind, even across removes.
R06: no stale snapshot - every call reads current storage; direct db.insert between calls is seen by apply and preview.

CONFLICT RESOLUTION: an older generated note claimed "preview may consume IDs and bool IDs are accepted". That note is unverified and superseded: preview NEVER consumes IDs (tested: test_preview_does_not_consume_ids, test_preview_on_error_consumes_nothing) and bool doc_ids are REJECTED (test_bool_doc_id_rejected). The happy-path smoke does not cover these boundaries; the tests above do.

R06: every call re-reads current storage - no stale initial snapshot; direct db.insert calls between apply/preview calls are seen by the wrapper. # HANDOFF - cachetools milestone 1

## Deliverable
`src/cachetools/tagged.py` implements `TaggedCache(maxsize)`, backed by
`cachetools.LRUCache` (via a private `_TaggedLRUCache` subclass that reports
evicted keys so tag memberships are cleaned up on eviction).

## Requirements status
- R01: put(key, value, tags=()) inserts/replaces; deep-copies values on input
  and get(); get() returns detached deep copy, KeyError on miss; tags must be
  a finite iterable of strings (bare str rejected, non-str entries rejected
  with ValueError, deduplicated, order preserved); all validation happens
  before any state mutation.
- R02: invalidate(tag) removes exactly entries carrying the tag and returns
  count; replacement removes old tag memberships; LRU eviction cleans
  memberships (no stale reuse); get() refreshes recency; len() counts live
  entries.
- R03: maxsize must be a positive int excluding bool (ValueError otherwise);
  invalid replacement input leaves old value/tags/recency unchanged (verified
  by tests); every value costs exactly one capacity slot.
- Claim-A extension (put_no_recency_refresh variant): overwriting an existing
  key via put refreshes LRU recency (it becomes MRU). Implemented and tested
  (test_replacement_refreshes_recency, test_replacement_refreshes_recency_with_tag_change).

## Design notes
- Internal state: `self.__data` (LRU storage), `self.__tags` (key -> tuple of
  tags), `self.__memberships` (tag -> list of keys).
- put() order: normalize tags -> hash-check key -> deepcopy value -> if
  existing: remove old memberships BEFORE LRU update (so an eviction during
  the update can never resurrect stale memberships) -> assign value/tags ->
  add new memberships. LRU __setitem__ moves key to MRU for both insert and
  replace.
- _TaggedLRUCache.popitem() calls self._on_evict(key) after LRUCache.popitem
  so evicted keys lose tag/tag-membership records.
- Also provides mapping-style helpers: __getitem__ (deep copy, refreshes
  recency), __delitem__, pop(key, default), clear(), maxsize/currsize
  properties, __contains__, __len__, __repr__.

## Tests
- Own tests: tests/test_tagged.py (23 tests, all pass).
- Public acceptance: acceptance_public.py (2 tests, pass).
- Upstream tests: tests/ (237 pass total incl. tagged; upstream files
  unchanged - git status shows only new files tagged.py/test_tagged.py).

Run: `PYTHONPATH=src:. python -m pytest tests/ acceptance_public.py -q`

# HANDOFF - cachetools milestones 1+2

## Deliverable
`src/cachetools/tagged.py` implements `TaggedCache(maxsize)`, backed by
`cachetools.LRUCache` (private `_TaggedLRUCache` subclass reports evicted
keys so tag memberships are cleaned up on eviction). All existing
cachetools APIs are untouched (upstream test files unchanged).

## Requirements status
- R01: put(key, value, tags=()) inserts/replaces; values deep-copied on
  input and on get(); get() returns detached deep copy, KeyError on miss;
  tags must be a finite iterable of strings (bare str and non-str entries
  raise ValueError before any state change); tags deduplicated, first-seen
  order preserved.
- R02: invalidate(tag) removes exactly matching entries, returns count;
  replacement removes old tag memberships; LRU eviction cleans
  memberships (no stale reuse of evicted keys); get() refreshes recency;
  len()/currsize count live entries.
- R03: maxsize positive int excluding bool (ValueError otherwise);
  invalid replacement input leaves old value/tags/recency unchanged;
  every value costs exactly one capacity slot.
- Claim-A (put refreshes recency): overwriting an existing key via put
  makes it MRU. Implemented and tested.
- R04: invalidate_many(tags, mode='any') - 'any' removes the union, 'all'
  removes entries containing every supplied tag; empty requested tags
  remove zero in either mode; returns number of distinct removed keys;
  invalid mode or tags raise ValueError before mutation; invalidate(tag)
  unchanged. Supersedes the old design note claiming 'empty all-tags
  matches every key'.
- R05: resize(maxsize) validates positive non-bool int first (failed resize
  preserves all state); shrinking evicts LRU entries, growing evicts
  nothing; surviving entries keep values, tag memberships, LRU order;
  maxsize property reports current capacity. Supersedes the old note that
  'resizing may flush the cache'.
- R06: generator tags accepted, consumed exactly once (verified with a
  counting generator); returned values detached across repeated gets and
  puts including nested lists/dicts.
- Claim-A round 2 (R05 expiry clarification): references R07/R08 expiry
  which are not part of the active requirements (no expiry feature exists
  in this milestone); resize preserves entire entry state as required. If
  expiry is added later, resize must preserve absolute expiry values.

## Design notes
- State: `self.__data` (LRU storage), `self.__tags` (key -> tuple of
  tags), `self.__memberships` (tag -> list of keys).
- put() order: normalize tags -> hash-check key -> deepcopy value -> if
  existing: remove old memberships BEFORE LRU update (eviction during the
  update can never resurrect stale memberships) -> assign value/tags ->
  add new memberships.
- resize() shrinks by calling self.__data.popitem() (LRU order) until
  len <= new maxsize, then updates both TaggedCache.__maxsize and the
  internal LRUCache capacity (`_Cache__maxsize`).
- invalidate_many('all') scans self.__tags; 'any' unions membership lists.

## Tests
- Own: tests/test_tagged.py (23) + tests/test_tagged_m2.py (20), all pass.
- Public acceptance: acceptance_public.py (3 tests, all pass incl.
  test_public_union_resize).
- Full suite: `PYTHONPATH=src:. python -m pytest tests/ acceptance_public.py -q`
  -> 259 passed, 0 failed.

# HANDOFF - cachetools milestones 1+2

## Deliverable
`src/cachetools/tagged.py` implements `TaggedCache(maxsize)`, backed by
`cachetools.LRUCache` (private `_TaggedLRUCache` subclass reports evicted
keys so tag memberships are cleaned up on eviction). All existing
cachetools APIs are untouched (upstream test files unchanged).

## Requirements status
- R01: put(key, value, tags=()) inserts/replaces; values deep-copied on
  input and on get(); get() returns detached deep copy, KeyError on miss;
  tags must be a finite iterable of strings (bare str and non-str entries
  raise ValueError before any state change); tags deduplicated, first-seen
  order preserved.
- R02: invalidate(tag) removes exactly matching entries, returns count;
  replacement removes old tag memberships; LRU eviction cleans
  memberships (no stale reuse of evicted keys); get() refreshes recency;
  len()/currsize count live entries.
- R03: maxsize positive int excluding bool (ValueError otherwise);
  invalid replacement input leaves old value/tags/recency unchanged;
  every value costs exactly one capacity slot.
- Claim-A (put refreshes recency): overwriting an existing key via put
  makes it MRU. Implemented and tested.
- R04: invalidate_many(tags, mode='any') - 'any' removes the union, 'all'
  removes entries containing every supplied tag; empty requested tags
  remove zero in either mode; returns number of distinct removed keys;
  invalid mode or tags raise ValueError before mutation; invalidate(tag)
  unchanged. Supersedes the old design note claiming 'empty all-tags
  matches every key'.
- R05: resize(maxsize) validates positive non-bool int first (failed resize
  preserves all state); shrinking evicts LRU entries, growing evicts
  nothing; surviving entries keep values, tag memberships, LRU order;
  maxsize property reports current capacity. Supersedes the old note that
  'resizing may flush the cache'.
- R06: generator tags accepted, consumed exactly once (verified with a
  counting generator); returned values detached across repeated gets and
  puts including nested lists/dicts.
- Claim-A round 2 (R05 expiry clarification): references R07/R08 expiry
  which are not part of the active requirements (no expiry feature exists
  in this milestone); resize preserves entire entry state as required. If
  expiry is added later, resize must preserve absolute expiry values.

## Design notes
- State: `self.__data` (LRU storage), `self.__tags` (key -> tuple of
  tags), `self.__memberships` (tag -> list of keys).
- put() order: normalize tags -> hash-check key -> deepcopy value -> if
  existing: remove old memberships BEFORE LRU update (eviction during the
  update can never resurrect stale memberships) -> assign value/tags ->
  add new memberships.
- resize() shrinks by calling self.__data.popitem() (LRU order) until
  len <= new maxsize, then updates both TaggedCache.__maxsize and the
  internal LRUCache capacity (`_Cache__maxsize`).
- invalidate_many('all') scans self.__tags; 'any' unions membership lists.

## Tests
- Own: tests/test_tagged.py (23) + tests/test_tagged_m2.py (20), all pass.
- Public acceptance: acceptance_public.py (3 tests, all pass incl.
  test_public_union_resize).
- Full suite: `PYTHONPATH=src:. python -m pytest tests/ acceptance_public.py -q`
  -> 259 passed, 0 failed.

  invalidate takes a single tag (A7); Claim-A extension active (A8).

  replace), re-open FR-010 and re-run convergence.
- Implementation must not touch upstream tests or acceptance_public.py.

# HANDOFF - cachetools TaggedCache (specs/001-transactions)

## Phase status
- constitution: done (.specify/memory/constitution.md v1.0.0, 2026-10-17)
- specify: done (specs/001-transactions/spec.md + checklists/requirements.md,
  all checklist items pass, 0 NEEDS CLARIFICATION; UPDATED 2026-10-17 for
  milestone 2 R04-R06 + round-2 R05 expiry clarification; FR-001..FR-021,
  SC-001..SC-008, A1-A11, User Stories 1-4, traceability table)
- plan: done (specs/001-transactions/plan.md; constitution gates PASS; additive
  src/cachetools/tagged.py + tests/test_tagged.py; upstream suite baseline
  216 passed under PYTHONPATH=src:.)
- tasks/implement/converge: pending

## Active requirements (frozen from milestone input, all retained)
- R01: put(key,value,tags=()) insert/replace; get returns detached deep copy or
  KeyError; values copied on input; hashable keys; tags = finite iterable of
  strings, deduplicated; bare string and non-string entries rejected with
  ValueError BEFORE any state change. -> FR-002..FR-004
- R02: invalidate(tag) removes exactly live entries carrying tag, returns count;
  replace removes old tag memberships; LRU eviction leaves no stale
  memberships; get refreshes recency; len counts live entries. -> FR-005..FR-009
- R02 extension (Claim-A, variant put_no_recency_refresh, 2026-09-21): put
  overwriting an existing key refreshes LRU recency (most-recently-used).
  Disposition (A8): active requirement FR-010; variant label is traceability
  only and does NOT override the refresh behavior.
- R03: maxsize positive integer excluding bool (ValueError otherwise); invalid
  replacement input leaves old value/tags/recency unchanged; each value costs
  one capacity slot regardless of size. -> FR-001, FR-011, FR-012
- R04 (milestone 2): invalidate_many(tags, mode='any'); mode='any' removes the
  union, mode='all' removes entries containing every supplied tag; empty
  requested tags remove ZERO entries in either mode (empty 'all' does NOT match
  every key); returns number of distinct removed keys; invalid mode or tags
  rejected with ValueError BEFORE mutation; invalidate(tag) remains compatible.
  -> FR-014..FR-016
- R05 (milestone 2): resize(maxsize) validates positive non-bool integer first;
  preserves surviving entries and their LRU order; shrinking evicts
  least-recently-used; growing does not evict; failed resize preserves all
  state; maxsize property reports current capacity. -> FR-017, FR-018
- R05 clarification (Claim-A round 2, 2026-09-22): preserving a surviving entry
  across resize preserves its ABSOLUTE expiry (R07/R08 define expiry as entry
  state); dropping expiries (immortal) or recomputing from resize time does not
  satisfy R05. -> FR-019 (binding when R07/R08 land; no expiry implemented yet,
  see A10)
- R06 (milestone 2): tags may be generators, consumed only once; returned
  values remain detached across repeated gets and puts incl. nested
  lists/dicts. -> FR-020, FR-021
- Preservation: all existing cachetools APIs unchanged; build on
  cachetools.LRUCache; upstream tests unchanged; acceptance_public.py is the
  public gate (do not modify). -> FR-013

## Conflicting evidence (superseded - do not rely on)
- Old generated design note: 'empty all-tags matches every key and resizing may
  flush the cache'. SUPERSEDED by R04/R05 (recorded as A9). Empty requested
  tags remove zero entries; resize never flushes the cache.

## Key assumptions (see spec.md A1-A11)
- Deep copy isolates nested containers (A1); put returns None (A2); tags
  materialized to finite string sequence, bare string rejected (A3); standard
  LRU recency incl. refresh on replace (A4); maxsize rejects 0/neg/bool/float
  (A5); additive module src/cachetools/tagged.py, no new deps (A6);
  invalidate single tag, compatible with invalidate_many([tag],'any') (A7);
  Claim-A extension active (A8); conflicting design note superseded (A9);
  R05 expiry clarification scoped to future R07/R08 (A10); invalidate_many
  dedupes request tags, count = distinct removed keys (A11).

## Unresolved / watch items
- R07/R08 (entry expiry) are referenced by the round-2 R05 clarification but
  are NOT part of the current milestone input: no expiry behavior is specified
  or implemented yet. FR-019 constrains any future expiry state; re-run
  specify/plan when R07/R08 arrive.
- If hidden acceptance contradicts A4/A8 (recency refresh on replace), re-open
  FR-010 and re-run convergence.
- Implementation must not touch upstream tests or acceptance_public.py.

# HANDOFF - cachetools TaggedCache (specs/001-transactions)

## Phase status
- constitution: done (.specify/memory/constitution.md v1.0.0, 2026-10-17)
- specify: done (specs/001-transactions/spec.md + checklists/requirements.md,
  all checklist items pass, 0 NEEDS CLARIFICATION; UPDATED 2026-10-17 for
  milestone 2 R04-R06 + round-2 R05 expiry clarification; FR-001..FR-021,
  SC-001..SC-008, A1-A11, User Stories 1-4, traceability table)
- plan: done (specs/001-transactions/plan.md; constitution gates PASS; additive
  src/cachetools/tagged.py + tests/test_tagged.py; upstream suite baseline
  216 passed under PYTHONPATH=src:.)
- tasks/implement/converge: pending

## Active requirements (frozen from milestone input, all retained)
- R01: put(key,value,tags=()) insert/replace; get returns detached deep copy or
  KeyError; values copied on input; hashable keys; tags = finite iterable of
  strings, deduplicated; bare string and non-string entries rejected with
  ValueError BEFORE any state change. -> FR-002..FR-004
- R02: invalidate(tag) removes exactly live entries carrying tag, returns count;
  replace removes old tag memberships; LRU eviction leaves no stale
  memberships; get refreshes recency; len counts live entries. -> FR-005..FR-009
- R02 extension (Claim-A, variant put_no_recency_refresh, 2026-09-21): put
  overwriting an existing key refreshes LRU recency (most-recently-used).
  Disposition (A8): active requirement FR-010; variant label is traceability
  only and does NOT override the refresh behavior.
- R03: maxsize positive integer excluding bool (ValueError otherwise); invalid
  replacement input leaves old value/tags/recency unchanged; each value costs
  one capacity slot regardless of size. -> FR-001, FR-011, FR-012
- R04 (milestone 2): invalidate_many(tags, mode='any'); mode='any' removes the
  union, mode='all' removes entries containing every supplied tag; empty
  requested tags remove ZERO entries in either mode (empty 'all' does NOT match
  every key); returns number of distinct removed keys; invalid mode or tags
  rejected with ValueError BEFORE mutation; invalidate(tag) remains compatible.
  -> FR-014..FR-016
- R05 (milestone 2): resize(maxsize) validates positive non-bool integer first;
  preserves surviving entries and their LRU order; shrinking evicts
  least-recently-used; growing does not evict; failed resize preserves all
  state; maxsize property reports current capacity. -> FR-017, FR-018
- R05 clarification (Claim-A round 2, 2026-09-22): preserving a surviving entry
  across resize preserves its ABSOLUTE expiry (R07/R08 define expiry as entry
  state); dropping expiries (immortal) or recomputing from resize time does not
  satisfy R05. -> FR-019 (binding when R07/R08 land; no expiry implemented yet,
  see A10)
- R06 (milestone 2): tags may be generators, consumed only once; returned
  values remain detached across repeated gets and puts incl. nested
  lists/dicts. -> FR-020, FR-021
- Preservation: all existing cachetools APIs unchanged; build on
  cachetools.LRUCache; upstream tests unchanged; acceptance_public.py is the
  public gate (do not modify). -> FR-013

## Conflicting evidence (superseded - do not rely on)
- Old generated design note: 'empty all-tags matches every key and resizing may
  flush the cache'. SUPERSEDED by R04/R05 (recorded as A9). Empty requested
  tags remove zero entries; resize never flushes the cache.

## Key assumptions (see spec.md A1-A11)
- Deep copy isolates nested containers (A1); put returns None (A2); tags
  materialized to finite string sequence, bare string rejected (A3); standard
  LRU recency incl. refresh on replace (A4); maxsize rejects 0/neg/bool/float
  (A5); additive module src/cachetools/tagged.py, no new deps (A6);
  invalidate single tag, compatible with invalidate_many([tag],'any') (A7);
  Claim-A extension active (A8); conflicting design note superseded (A9);
  R05 expiry clarification scoped to future R07/R08 (A10); invalidate_many
  dedupes request tags, count = distinct removed keys (A11); TTL value class
  and absolute-expiry computation (A12); purge/recency non-interference (A13).

## Milestone 3 (R07/R08) - specify phase updated 2026-10-17
- R07/R08 ARE now active requirements (milestone 3 retains R01-R06).
  Spec.md updated: User Story 5 (TTL), FR-022..FR-028, SC-009/SC-010,
  edge cases, Key Entities (Entry expiry, Timer), Assumptions A12/A13,
  traceability rows for R07/R08. Checklist re-validated (all pass).
- FR-019 (round-2 R05 clarification) is now fully in scope: resize MUST
  preserve each surviving entry's absolute expiry; must not drop expiries or
  recompute them from resize time. FR-026 purge happens before resize and
  does not recompute surviving expiries (consistent).
- R07: timer=None default time.monotonic; put ttl=None (no expiry) or finite
  nonnegative int/float excluding bool -> expiry = timer()+ttl; invalid TTL
  ValueError before mutation; ttl=0 immediately expired; exact boundary
  (timer()==expiry) is expired (inclusive).
- R08: purge expired before get/put/len/resize/invalidation without touching
  survivor recency; overwrite replaces prior expiry; invalidation counts only
  live entries; missing/expired get raises KeyError; no-timer/ttl callers
  unchanged.
- If hidden acceptance contradicts A4/A8 (recency refresh on replace), re-open
  FR-010 and re-run convergence.
- Implementation must not touch upstream tests or acceptance_public.py.

## Next actions
- $speckit-tasks, then implement in src/cachetools/tagged.py with
  project-authored tests (tests/test_tagged.py); verify via
  `PYTHONPATH=src:. python3 -m pytest acceptance_public.py tests/test_tagged.py
  tests/ -q` and the milestone falsification cases (empty 'all' removes 0;
  resize shrink evicts LRU only; generator consumed once; failed resize no-op).

# HANDOFF — tinydb milestone 1 (001-transactions)

Phase state: **plan complete** (spec -> plan done; tasks/implement pending).

## Deliverables so far
- `specs/001-transactions/plan.md` — filled plan (Technical Context, Constitution
  Check PASS, project structure, complexity tracking empty).
- `specs/001-transactions/research.md` — decisions D1-D6 (snapshot/restore
  rollback, ValueError for missing-ID remove, deepcopy on insert, two-phase
  validation, test run command, module surface).
- `specs/001-transactions/data-model.md`, `specs/001-transactions/contracts/batchwriter.md`,
  `specs/001-transactions/quickstart.md` — Phase 1 artifacts.
- This file (assumptions + evidence, constitution V).

## Assumptions (A1-A7 from spec.md, status)
- A1 `doc_id` positive int, bools rejected — open assumption, encoded in
  validation (research D4).
- A2 missing-ID remove error type — **resolved**: `ValueError`, pinned by
  `acceptance_public.py::test_public_atomic` (research D2).
- A3 rollback restores the complete pre-batch default-table data (not just
  inverse ops) — open assumption, implemented via deepcopy snapshot (D1).
- A4 `apply` returns only inserted IDs (ints), in insertion order — open
  assumption, pinned by `acceptance_public.py::test_public_basic`.
- A5 default table only; no multi-table, no concurrency — open assumption,
  out of contract per contracts/batchwriter.md.
- A6 `operations` must be a `list` (not arbitrary iterable) — open assumption,
  ValueError otherwise (R01 wording "accepts a list").
- A7 no re-export of `BatchWriter` from `tinydb/__init__.py` — open
  assumption (D6); import path is `tinydb.journal`.

## Design notes for implementation (converge phase)
- `BatchWriter.__init__(db)` stores `self._db`; `apply(operations)`:
  1. validate all ops (list; dict ops; op in {insert,remove}; insert needs
     dict `document`; remove needs int `doc_id` > 0, `bool` excluded) ->
     `ValueError` before any mutation;
  2. `snapshot = deepcopy(table._read_table())` (table = `db.table('_default')`);
  3. apply sequentially: insert -> `doc_id = table.insert(deepcopy(document))`,
     collect IDs; remove -> if `doc_id not in table._read_table()` raise
     `ValueError`, else `table.remove(doc_ids=[doc_id])`;
  4. on ANY exception during step 3: restore via
     `table._update_table(lambda t: (t.clear(), t.update(snapshot)))` (single
     storage write), clear the table query cache, re-raise.
- Tables read storage on every access (verified in `tinydb/table.py`), so
  previously acquired handles observe success and rollback automatically.
- Upstream `Table.insert` does only a shallow `dict(document)`; the deepcopy
  in step 3 is what satisfies R03 aliasing.

## Evidence (observed commands, 2026-10-17)
- `python3 .specify/scripts/python/setup_plan.py --json` -> copied plan
  template; FEATURE_DIR=/testbed/specs/001-transactions (ref
  13fb7876237a28c4af66def5db23362b84550004c5b4f7ae3eadcfb31ebfd01a).
- `python3 -m pytest -q -o addopts="" tests/` -> `223 passed in 1.25s`
  (upstream baseline; pytest.ini addopts need pytest-cov, not installed).
- `python3 -m pytest -q -o addopts="" acceptance_public.py` -> collection
  error `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'tinydb.journal'` (expected
  pre-implementation state).
- `ls .specify/` -> no `extensions.yml` (hooks skipped per skill rules).
- Source reads: `tinydb/table.py` (`insert`, `insert_multiple`, `remove`,
  `_get_next_id`, `_read_table`, `_update_table`), `tinydb/database.py`
  (`table()`, `default_table_name='_default'`), `tinydb/storages.py` (Storage
  read/write), `acceptance_public.py` (full), `.specify/memory/constitution.md`.

## Unresolved gaps
- None blocking plan. Implementation phase must: create `tinydb/journal.py`,
  add `tests/test_journal.py`, rerun quickstart scenarios, and record evidence
  for R01-R03 (own tests + `acceptance_public.py` + upstream 223 unchanged).

- A2 missing-ID remove error type — **resolved**: `ValueError`, pinned by
  `acceptance_public.py::test_public_atomic` (research D2).
- A3 rollback restores the complete pre-batch default-table data (not just
  inverse ops) — open assumption, implemented via deepcopy snapshot (D1).
- A4 `apply` returns only inserted IDs (ints), in insertion order — open
  assumption, pinned by `acceptance_public.py::test_public_basic`.
- A5 default table only; no multi-table, no concurrency — open assumption,
  out of contract per contracts/batchwriter.md.
- A6 `operations` must be a `list` (not arbitrary iterable) — open assumption,
  ValueError otherwise (R01 wording "accepts a list").
- A7 no re-export of `BatchWriter` from `tinydb/__init__.py` — open
  assumption (D6); import path is `tinydb.journal`.

## Design notes for implementation (converge phase)
- `BatchWriter.__init__(db)` stores `self._db`; `apply(operations)`:
  1. validate all ops (list; dict ops; op in {insert,remove}; insert needs
     dict `document`; remove needs int `doc_id` > 0, `bool` excluded) ->
     `ValueError` before any mutation;
  2. `snapshot = deepcopy(table._read_table())` (table = `db.table('_default')`);
  3. apply sequentially: insert -> `doc_id = table.insert(deepcopy(document))`,
     collect IDs; remove -> if `doc_id not in table._read_table()` raise
     `ValueError`, else `table.remove(doc_ids=[doc_id])`;
  4. on ANY exception during step 3: restore via
     `table._update_table(lambda t: (t.clear(), t.update(snapshot)))` (single
     storage write), clear the table query cache, re-raise.
- Tables read storage on every access (verified in `tinydb/table.py`), so
  previously acquired handles observe success and rollback automatically.
- Upstream `Table.insert` does only a shallow `dict(document)`; the deepcopy
  in step 3 is what satisfies R03 aliasing.

# HANDOFF — tinydb milestone 1 (001-transactions)

Phase state: **plan complete** (spec -> plan done; tasks/implement pending).

## Deliverables so far
- `specs/001-transactions/plan.md` — filled plan (Technical Context, Constitution
  Check PASS, project structure, complexity tracking empty).
- `specs/001-transactions/research.md` — decisions D1-D6 (snapshot/restore
  rollback, ValueError for missing-ID remove, deepcopy on insert, two-phase
  validation, test run command, module surface).
- `specs/001-transactions/data-model.md`, `specs/001-transactions/contracts/batchwriter.md`,
  `specs/001-transactions/quickstart.md` — Phase 1 artifacts.
- This file (assumptions + evidence, constitution V).

## Assumptions (A1-A7 from spec.md, status)
- A1 `doc_id` positive int, bools rejected — open assumption, encoded in
  validation (research D4).
- A2 missing-ID remove error type — **resolved**: `ValueError`, pinned by
  `acceptance_public.py::test_public_atomic` (research D2).
- A3 rollback restores the complete pre-batch default-table data (not just
  inverse ops) — open assumption, implemented via deepcopy snapshot (D1).
- A4 `apply` returns only inserted IDs (ints), in insertion order — open
  assumption, pinned by `acceptance_public.py::test_public_basic`.
- A5 default table only; no multi-table, no concurrency — open assumption,
  out of contract per contracts/batchwriter.md.
- A6 `operations` must be a `list` (not arbitrary iterable) — open assumption,
  ValueError otherwise (R01 wording "accepts a list").
- A7 no re-export of `BatchWriter` from `tinydb/__init__.py` — open
  assumption (D6); import path is `tinydb.journal`.

## Design notes for implementation (converge phase)
- `BatchWriter.__init__(db)` stores `self._db`; `apply(operations)`:
  1. validate all ops (list; dict ops; op in {insert,remove}; insert needs
     dict `document`; remove needs int `doc_id` > 0, `bool` excluded) ->
     `ValueError` before any mutation;
  2. `snapshot = deepcopy(table._read_table())` (table = `db.table('_default')`);
  3. apply sequentially: insert -> `doc_id = table.insert(deepcopy(document))`,
     collect IDs; remove -> if `doc_id not in table._read_table()` raise
     `ValueError`, else `table.remove(doc_ids=[doc_id])`;
  4. on ANY exception during step 3: restore via
     `table._update_table(lambda t: (t.clear(), t.update(snapshot)))` (single
     storage write), clear the table query cache, re-raise.
- Tables read storage on every access (verified in `tinydb/table.py`), so
  previously acquired handles observe success and rollback automatically.
- Upstream `Table.insert` does only a shallow `dict(document)`; the deepcopy
  in step 3 is what satisfies R03 aliasing.

    not consumed, invalid token, returned-list mutation isolation

    bookkeeping is in-memory, instance-scoped, not persisted)
- `specs/001-transactions/checklists/requirements.md` — re-validated, all items
  [x]; FR-001..FR-016 map to R01/R02/R03, R04, R05, R05b, R05-clarification,

## Conflict resolution (recorded in spec A8)
Older unverified note "preview may consume IDs and bool IDs are accepted" is
superseded by R04/R05 (bool doc_ids rejected; preview never consumes IDs).
Happy-path smoke alone does not verify those boundaries.

## Key contract points for plan/implement (converge phase)
- `tinydb/journal.py::BatchWriter(db)`; default table only; ordinary APIs untouched.
- apply(operations, token=None): structural validation BEFORE any commit
  (list ops; dict ops; op in {insert, remove}; insert -> dict document
  (empty dict OK); remove -> int doc_id > 0, bool rejected; no unsupported
  fields) -> ValueError.
- Atomicity: snapshot pre-batch default-table data; sequential apply; on ANY
  error restore complete pre-batch data (single coherent write so previously
  acquired db.table('_default') handles observe success AND rollback; keep
  query caches coherent).
- ID sequence: successful batch advances next-insertion-ID state and writes it
  back to the underlying table (direct db.insert continues without reuse or
  rewind, even across removes); failed batch/preview never consume IDs.
- preview(operations): single-argument signature; returns new detached list of
  IDs apply would produce; no data/ID-state changes; on error raises the same
  error apply would raise (ValueError for structural; missing-ID remove is an
  error) without consuming IDs.
- Deep-copy on insert: stored docs and returned data must not alias caller
  input (nested).
- R07: token is nonempty string or None; invalid -> ValueError; successful
  (token, ops) recorded on the instance; identical replay returns detached
  copy of original IDs, no rerun, even after other direct writes; same token
  + different ops -> ValueError, no data change; failed batch does not consume
  token. Value-equality on validated ops (A10).
- R08: bookkeeping in-memory on the instance, never in user documents; preview
  never records/consumes tokens; returned lists must not expose bookkeeping
  through mutation.
- acceptance_public.py pins: apply insert-> [1], remove-> [], atomic rollback
  (ValueError), preview [1] with empty table then apply [1], token replay
  [1] twice with len(db)==1.
